title_prefix: ms-parse never checks fragment arity: ex
mechanism: ms-parse splits a fragment's argument list on top-level commas and hands the whole list to make-ms-node without ever checking its length (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1180-1190). ms-compute-type reads only x, y and z and ms-node-script only (sub 0) and (sub 1), so a THIRD argument to and_v/and_b/or_b/or_c/or_d/or_i, a FOURTH to andor, a second key to pk()/pk_k()/pkh(), or a second number to older()/after() is dropped, and the node types, prints and COMPILES as though it had not been written. Only and_n and thresh check (:1187, :1193). In the other direction a missing argument leaves (nth 1 subs) NIL and every downstream walker dereferences it. Core's Parse pushes an exact ParseContext schedule per fragment -- CLOSE_BRACKET, WRAPPED_EXPR, COMMA, WRAPPED_EXPR for the binary combinators (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:2072-2090) and one more WRAPPED_EXPR/COMMA pair for andor (:2065-2071) -- and CLOSE_BRACKET fails unless the next character is ')' while COMMA fails unless it is ',' (:2187-2196), so and_v(X,Y,Z) dies at the CLOSE_BRACKET that meets the third comma and and_v(X) dies at the COMMA that meets ')'. ComputeType additionally CHECK_NONFATALs n_subs per fragment (miniscript.cpp:60-71).
consequence: A descriptor string Core refuses is accepted here as a DIFFERENT, strictly weaker policy, and the weakening reaches the ADDRESS: wsh(and_v(v:pk(A),older(10),pk(B))) and wsh(and_v(v:pk(A),older(10))) produce the identical scriptPubKey, so coins sent to the address the operator believes requires B are in fact governed by A-plus-timelock alone. The shipped signer then completes such a spend with a strict subset of the written keys. Nothing on the accept path warns; only re-reading the normalized string from getdescriptorinfo reveals the dropped argument. In the too-few-arguments direction the descriptor RPCs answer -32603 'Internal error' from a raw Lisp TYPE-ERROR (src/rpc/server.lisp:1151-1157 maps any non-rpc-error condition to +rpc-internal-error+ and HTTP 500) instead of Core's parse error. Kept at S2 rather than raised: it is a wrong answer an operator acts on, and the residual funds risk needs a second event (a compromised subset of the intended signers) before coins actually move.
evidence: Container: /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s2, warm image, build/ga11probe/p4.lisp and p4b.lisp. Extra arguments dropped, ms-parse :p2wsh -- and_v(v:pk(K1),older(10),pk(K2)) normalizes to 'and_v(v:pk(K1),older(10))' with script 2103d30199...ad5ab2, byte-identical to the two-argument form's script; andor(0,1,1,pk(K)) -> 'andor(0,1,1)'; or_i(0,1,pk(K)) -> 'l:1'; pk(K1,K2) -> 'pk(K1)'; older(10,99) -> 'older(10)'. The address is the weaker policy's: wsh(and_v(v:pk(K1),older(10),pk(K2))) and wsh(and_v(v:pk(K1),older(10))) both expand to scriptPubKey 0020b8a2cf88fd7d0b4c4d4f164dd1eadffe5e6e6e385fcfd6312738df2b6e948352 and both print as the two-argument form. What the satisfier does with the dropped argument, through the shipped bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method 'signrawtransactionwithkey': the witnessScript compiled from and_v(v:pk(A),pk(B),pk(C)) equals the one compiled from and_v(v:pk(A),pk(B)) byte for byte (2103a34b99...ad2103669b8a...ac) and signs complete:true holding only A and B, while the genuine three-key policy and_v(v:pk(A),and_v(v:pk(B),pk(C))) with the same two keys is complete:false. Too few arguments: parse-descriptor of wsh(and_v(v:pk(K))), wsh(or_b(pk(K))), wsh(andor(1,1)) and wsh(thresh(1,pk(K),and_v(v:pk(K)))) each raised TYPE-ERROR 'The value NIL is not of type BITCOIN-LISP.VALIDATION::MS-NODE', and dispatch-rpc-method 'getdescriptorinfo' on wsh(and_v(v:pk(A))) raised the same raw TYPE-ERROR out of the handler. Core's rejection of both directions read from refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:2072-2090 (the schedule) and :2187-2196 (COMMA / CLOSE_BRACKET).
fix_shape: Check arity where Core checks it, in the parser, and make it a parse failure rather than a type failure. The faithful port is Core's ParseContext schedule: after each combinator's declared number of WRAPPED_EXPRs, require exactly ')' and fail on anything else, so a surplus comma and a missing one are both parse errors at the same place. Short of restructuring ms-parse into Core's explicit stack, the equivalent is a per-fragment required-argument-count table consulted before make-ms-node -- and_v/and_b/or_b/or_c/or_d/or_i exactly 2, andor exactly 3, and_n exactly 2 (already checked), pk/pk_k/pkh/pk_h/older/after/sha256/hash256/ripemd160/hash160 exactly 1, thresh at least 2 (already checked), multi/multi_a at least 2 -- signalling miniscript-parse-error so the descriptor layer reports Core's message and the RPC answers a parse error instead of -32603. Mirror Core's ComputeType n_subs CHECK_NONFATALs (miniscript.cpp:60-71) as an internal assertion so a future construction site cannot re-open the hole from the other side, and add a test that ms-node-to-string of every parsed expression re-parses to the SAME script, which is the property the dropped argument violated.
